props.title: Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead

sections.content: Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead emerged during the post-Tarantino crime film boom, but brings its own distinct neo-noir style. Director Gary Fleder and writer Scott Rosenberg craft a morality tale that feels like a spiritual successor to Miller's Crossing (1990), with Andy Garcia's Jimmy "The Saint" Tosnia leading a crew of memorable misfits including Christopher Walken, Christopher Lloyd, and Treat Williams. Like The Usual Suspects (1995) from the same year, it plays with crime film conventions while adding philosophical weight about loyalty, redemption and facing death with dignity.

sections.content: The film's distinctive slang vocabulary ("boat drinks," "buckwheats," "give it a name") follows in the tradition of hard-boiled noir dialogue from The Big Sleep (1946) and Sweet Smell of Success (1957). This artificial criminal argot would later influence films like Brick (2005), which transplanted noir speech patterns to a high school setting. The film's mix of violence and philosophy also presaged later crime dramas like In Bruges (2008) and The Way of the Gun (2000).

Christopher Walken's performance as the paralyzed crime boss Mr. Shhh creates one of the most memorable villains of 90s crime cinema. His methodical, poetic menace recalls his work in King of New York (1990) while pointing toward later roles in True Romance (1993) and Seven Psychopaths (2012). The film's fatalistic tone and focus on honor among criminals clearly influenced later works like Lucky Number Slevin (2006). SUBHEAD: Neo-Noir Revival Impact

sections.content: While not a major box office success, Things to Do in Denver When You're Dead helped cement several neo-noir trends of the 1990s: elaborate criminal codes of conduct, philosophical hitmen, and fatalistic plotting. These elements would appear in films like The Boondock Saints (1999) and The Salton Sea (2002). The film's religious imagery and themes of redemption through violence also influenced later crime dramas like The Devil's Rejects (2005).
